description: Defines how A.R.I.A. identifies, resolves, represents, scores, inherits, changes, and applies technical context without depending on rigid directory hierarchies.

core_principle.statement: Context is a multidimensional technical state, not a directory path. ARIA shall identify the combination of entities, relationships, conditions, scope, participants, and time required to determine which knowledge and experience apply to the current reasoning problem.
rules: Context shall be represented as intersecting dimensions rather than one hierarchical folder path.
A technical entity may participate in many contexts simultaneously.
Missing context shall remain explicitly unknown.
Context shall not be invented merely to complete a structure.
Context may change during a case.
Context determines applicability but does not itself establish diagnosis.
Context resolution shall remain traceable to evidence or authoritative records.

multidimensional_model.description: Context shall be represented as a set of dimensions and graph relationships rather than a single path.
multidimensional_model.interpretation: Each value references a reusable graph entity. The complete context exists as the intersection of those entities rather than as a directory named Nokia/Wavence/UBT-T/18GHz/2+0/Space-Diversity/Commissioning/Site-A/Radio-B/Diversity.

context_resolution_pipeline.name: EXTRACT_CANDIDATE_CONTEXT
context_resolution_pipeline.description: Identify context stated or implied by user input, case records, artifacts, equipment data, and project information.

context_resolution_pipeline.name: NORMALIZE_TERMS
context_resolution_pipeline.description: Resolve aliases, abbreviations, informal names, and manufacturer terminology to canonical entities.

context_resolution_pipeline.name: RESOLVE_GRAPH_ENTITIES
context_resolution_pipeline.description: Map normalized terms to existing knowledge graph entities.

context_resolution_pipeline.name: APPLY_RELATIONSHIP_CONSTRAINTS
context_resolution_pipeline.description: Check whether resolved context combinations are technically compatible.

context_resolution_pipeline.name: IDENTIFY_MISSING_CONTEXT
context_resolution_pipeline.description: Determine which unresolved dimensions could materially affect reasoning.

context_resolution_pipeline.name: CALCULATE_CONTEXT_CONFIDENCE
context_resolution_pipeline.description: Estimate confidence that the current context representation is correct.

context_resolution_pipeline.name: PUBLISH_CONTEXT_STATE
context_resolution_pipeline.description: Provide the resolved context to memory, retrieval, hypothesis, probability, evidence, and routing engines.

rules: Aliases shall map to canonical entities rather than create duplicate technical entities.
Ambiguous aliases shall not be silently resolved without sufficient context.
Manufacturer terminology may override generic terminology only within applicable scope.
Alias mappings shall preserve provenance.

context_inheritance.description: Applicable knowledge may inherit through graph relationships when the more specific entity does not override the broader rule.

example.general: RSL degradation may result from physical RF path loss.
example.manufacturer: Nokia equipment uses applicable manufacturer-specific measurements and alarms.
example.product: UBT-T adds product-specific ports and configuration relationships.
example.variant: 18 GHz variant adds frequency-specific hardware and engineering constraints.

rules: General technical knowledge remains available unless a more specific rule limits applicability.
Specific knowledge may refine broader knowledge.
Specific knowledge shall not duplicate broader knowledge unnecessarily.
Overrides shall be explicit.
Inheritance shall preserve the source level of each applicable rule.
Applicability shall be calculated relative to the knowledge, experience, evidence, hypothesis, or action being evaluated.
Not every context dimension matters equally to every technical concept.
Missing irrelevant context shall not reduce applicability.
Conflict in a critical context dimension may reduce applicability sharply.

critical_context.description: Different technical questions require different minimum context.

examples.technical_question: What is the expected free-space path loss?
Which UBT-T port should the Diversity flex connect to?
How likely is this technician's configuration to contain an error?

rules: ARIA shall request missing context only when it materially affects the reasoning operation.
ARIA shall not interrogate the user for dimensions irrelevant to the current question.

context_signature.description: A normalized context signature may be used for indexing and historical aggregation without becoming a directory path.
rules: Signatures may contain only dimensions relevant to the indexed pattern.
Different learning aggregates may use different context signatures.
A signature shall reference canonical entity identifiers when implemented.
Signatures shall not require every possible context dimension.
Greater specificity may improve applicability but may reduce available historical sample size.
Reasoning engines shall balance specificity against statistical support.
ARIA shall be capable of broadening context when specific historical data is sparse.
Material context changes shall create a new context version.
Previous context versions shall remain historical.
Probability and routing engines shall be notified when material context changes.
Previously applicable evidence or knowledge may require reevaluation after a context change.

relationship_context.description: Some technical meaning exists in relationships rather than individual entities.
rules: ARIA shall preserve relationship context when the technical fact depends on how entities interact.
A component shall not be interpreted only from its category.
Connection, direction, role, dependency, and temporal relationships may materially change technical meaning.

examples: User reports UBT-T while project inventory identifies UBT.
Screenshot indicates Radio A while conversation refers to Radio B.
Historical case is 11 GHz while current case is 18 GHz.
Documentation applies to firmware version different from current equipment.
rules: Material context conflicts shall not be silently resolved.
ARIA shall determine whether one source supersedes another or whether clarification is required.
Context conflict shall reduce applicability confidence.
Reasoning based on uncertain context shall communicate material uncertainty.

new_product_integration.description: New products shall integrate by adding entities and relationships rather than requiring redesign of the directory structure.
new_product_integration.rule: A new product shall reuse existing applicable technical concepts and add only the relationships and concepts that are genuinely new.

redundancy_prevention.description: Technical concepts shall be normalized into reusable graph entities rather than repeatedly rewritten under every applicable manufacturer, product, and procedure.
rules: One canonical concept may have many relationships.
Manufacturer-specific behavior shall be represented as additional relationships or scoped properties.
Product-specific exceptions shall be explicit rather than implemented through duplicated general knowledge.

engine_interfaces.knowledge_graph: Uses context to determine which technical nodes and relationships apply.
engine_interfaces.memory_engine: Uses context to retrieve relevant memory.
engine_interfaces.hypothesis_engine: Uses context to generate technically compatible hypotheses.
engine_interfaces.probability_engine: Uses context to select applicable historical populations and priors.
engine_interfaces.evidence_engine: Uses context to determine evidence applicability.
engine_interfaces.routing_engine: Uses context to determine valid and useful diagnostic actions.
engine_interfaces.learning_engine: Uses context to preserve the scope of learned experience.

semantic_rules.rule: Context is multidimensional and shall not be represented as one mandatory hierarchical directory.
Technical concepts shall be shared across contexts rather than duplicated merely because they apply to multiple products or manufacturers.
Manufacturer-specific and product-specific knowledge shall refine shared technical concepts through scoped relationships.
Missing context shall remain unknown rather than being silently assumed.
ARIA shall request missing context only when obtaining it is expected to materially improve reasoning.
Context resolution shall preserve provenance.
A context value may be reported, inferred, or confirmed, and these states shall remain distinguishable.
Context applicability is relative to the technical question being evaluated.
More specific context shall not automatically override broader knowledge when the specific evidence is weak or inapplicable.
ARIA shall balance contextual specificity against available statistical support.
Material context changes shall trigger reevaluation of affected hypotheses, probabilities, evidence applicability, and routes.
Historical context versions shall remain available for reconstruction.
Relationships between entities may be as important as the entities themselves.
New products shall extend the graph rather than require restructuring existing knowledge.
Aliases shall resolve to canonical entities rather than create duplicate technical concepts.
Context conflict shall reduce confidence and shall not be hidden.
The same failure mode may apply across many contexts while having different probabilities or diagnostic routes within each.
Context determines applicability; evidence determines the current technical state.
The language model may assist in extracting candidate context, but authoritative context resolution shall be controlled by structured ARIA services.
ARIA's context architecture shall support growth without requiring exponential duplication of technical knowledge.
